extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, in-house counsel, USPTO officials, and policy makers reviewing the Patent Reform Act of 2007
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the substantive legal standards, procedural requirements, and evaluative criteria introduced or changed by the Patent Reform Act of 2007 as described in the Committee report and legislative history. Focuses on filing rules, patentability timing, damages, willfulness, USPTO procedures, and related provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor / applicant conduct with the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be honest and forthcoming in their dealings with the USPTO; rules governing such conduct should not chill meaningful disclosures to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New section 298 is intended to balance the need for candor with protection against chilling disclosures to the Office. (Context: statement of principle; no specific sanction text in this chunk.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Director authority to accept late filings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may accept late-filed applications or other filings if the filer satisfies the Director that the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request must be filed within 30 days of the missed deadline and must demonstrate the delay was unintentional. The Director has discretion to grant such requests and the decision is not appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on remedies for methods required by statute (Check 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practicing a check imaging and archival method or system that is called for under the Check 21 Act shall not constitute patent infringement for purposes of certain remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 14 amends 35 U.S.C. §287 to limit remedies available against a financial institution with respect to check imaging/archival methods required by the Check 21 Act; applies to any civil action pending or filed on or after enactment. Does not affect other uses of those methods or systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO fee retention and revolving fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a revolving fund permitting the USPTO to retain the fees it collects rather than rely on annual appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting, notification, and auditing requirements accompany the fund to assure fiscal discipline, responsibility, and accountability. Rationale: reduce backlog and pendency by linking collected fees to USPTO expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and rule of construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided, the Act takes effect 12 months after enactment and applies to any patent issued on or after that effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provides that enactment of section 102(b)(3) is intended to promote joint research activities consistent with the CREATE Act and should be administered consistently with that intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to first-inventor-to-file priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States patent system is converted to a first-inventor-to-file system giving priority to the earlier-filed application for a claimed invention; interference proceedings are replaced with derivation proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference procedures are repealed; derivation proceedings determine whether an earlier-filed applicant was the proper applicant. Various conforming amendments to Secs. 100, 102, 103, 120, 135, and repeal of Secs. 104 and 157 are made to effect the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year grace period for inventor disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-year grace period is provided for an inventor or joint inventor that discloses the subject matter of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under amended Sec. 102(a)(1), patents shall not issue if the invention was publicly available more than a year before filing; the inventor's own disclosures within the prior year do not bar patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to prior art for inventor-originated disclosures and common ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter that would otherwise be prior art is not prior art if, before the disclosure, it had been publicly disclosed by the inventor or was obtained from the inventor; also, prior art under certain subsections is excused if the subject matter was owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended Sec. 102(b) provides exception where subject matter was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor, previously disclosed by the inventor, or where the subject matter and claimed invention were owned by the same person prior to the effective filing date. The CREATE Act exception for joint research agreements is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation proceeding requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A derivation proceeding may be requested to determine whether an earlier applicant derived the claimed invention and filed without authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must set forth the basis for finding derivation and be filed within 12 months of the date of first publication of an application for a substantially same claim. The Board issues a final decision; Board decisions may be appealed to the Federal Circuit or to district court under Sec. 146.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements and consequences for substitute inventor's statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 115 is amended to permit an applicant to submit a substitute statement in lieu of the inventor's oath or declaration in specified circumstances (e.g., inventor unable or unwilling and under obligation to assign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply will not be a basis for invalidity or unenforceability if remedied by a supplemental and corrected statement. False substitute statements are subject to the same penalties as false oaths and declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a patent application (assignee/proprietary interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend section 118 to allow the person to whom the inventor has assigned (or is under an obligation to assign) the invention, or a person showing sufficient proprietary interest, to file a patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change is intended to make it easier for patent owners to file applications and preserve rights of the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court award of damages: baseline and reasonable royalty floor
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall award damages adequate to compensate for infringement but not less than a reasonable royalty, together with interest and costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The court may receive expert testimony to assist in determining damages. Methods for calculating reasonable royalty are specified and the court should identify relevant factors for the chosen method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire market value rule (method A for reasonable royalty)
rubrics_metrics.description: A royalty may be based upon the entire market value of the larger apparatus/process incorporating the infringing product/process if the claimed invention's specific contribution over the prior art is the predominant basis for market demand of the larger apparatus/process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits use of the entire market value rule to situations where the patented feature predominantly drives demand for the whole product/process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Established marketplace licensing method (method B for reasonable royalty)
rubrics_metrics.description: A royalty may be based on other nonexclusive licenses of the patented invention if the claimed invention has been the subject of nonexclusive licenses to a number of persons sufficient to indicate general marketplace recognition, the license was secured prior to filing of the case, and the infringer's use is of substantially the same scope, volume and benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This method relies on comparable licensing evidence that predates the litigation and matches the infringer's use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment requirement (method C/backstop for reasonable royalty)
rubrics_metrics.description: If showings under (A) and (B) have not been made, the court shall conduct an analysis to ensure a reasonable royalty is applied only to the portion of the economic value of the infringing product or process properly attributable to the claimed invention's specific contribution over the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to prevent overcompensation by requiring apportionment of value attributable to the claimed invention versus preexisting elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valuation of combination inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: For a combination invention with elements individually present in the prior art, the contribution over the prior art may include value of additional function from the combination and enhanced value of prior art elements as part of the combination, if the patentee demonstrates that value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may consider both new function and enhancement of known elements when apportioning value; patentee bears burden to demonstrate such value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court consideration of other relevant factors in reasonable royalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appropriate, the court may consider (or direct the jury to consider) any other relevant factors under applicable law when determining a reasonable royalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The listed methods apply only to reasonable royalty calculation, but do not preclude other relevant evidence or factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willful infringement: damage enhancement and judge-only determination
rubrics_metrics.description: A court may increase damages by up to three times based on a finding of willful infringement. A determination of willful infringement shall be made without a jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Willfulness is codified and changed; enhancement capped at 3x and is a bench determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willful infringement: elements to prove by clear and convincing evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove willful infringement, a patentee must prove by clear and convincing evidence one of: (A) the infringer received written notice detailing alleged acts with particularity and thereafter infringed after reasonable opportunity to investigate; (B) after notice and investigation, the infringer intentionally copied the invention with knowledge it was patented; or (C) after a court finding of infringement, the infringer engaged in conduct not colorably different causing a separate finding of infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute specifies three alternative bases for willfulness, all requiring strong proof and particular factual showings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on willful infringement findings — good faith defense
rubrics_metrics.description: A court may not find willful infringement for any period during which the infringer had an informed good faith belief that the patent was invalid or unenforceable, or would not be infringed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An informed good faith belief may be established by (a) reasonable reliance on advice of counsel; (b) evidence that the infringer sought to modify conduct to avoid infringement after discovering the patent; or (c) other sufficient evidence. The infringer's decision not to present advice of counsel is not relevant to willfulness determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on willful infringement findings — timing of pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may not plead (and a court may not determine) willful infringement before a court determines that the patent is not invalid, is enforceable, and has been infringed by the infringer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents early willfulness claims before threshold issues (validity, enforceability, infringement) have been adjudicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on past damages (marking and notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: For patented inventions not covered under subsection (a)(1) of Sec. 287, past damages are limited to 2 years prior to filing of a complaint (or counterclaim) except upon proof that the infringer was notified of the infringement; liability for past damages in no case shall exceed 6 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 287 is renumbered; this change narrows the period for which past damages are recoverable absent notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanded prior user rights (affiliates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsection (b)(6) of Sec. 273 is amended to allow 'affiliates' of the person who performed the necessary prior user rights acts to assert the defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadens who may assert the prior user rights defense to include related corporate entities that performed the acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior user rights study requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 2 years of enactment, the Director shall report to Congress findings and recommendations regarding the operation of 'prior user rights' in selected countries compared to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates comparative study to inform potential future legislative changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of amended provisions to civil actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendments made by various sections shall apply to any civil action commenced on or after the date of enactment of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified application dates are provided for fairness and transitional purposes; some provisions may have different effective dates where noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review (PGR) initiation standards and limits (manager's amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manager's and subsequent amendments modified PGR initiation standards, including raising the standard (in some versions to 'substantial new question of patentability'), making denials discretionary and not reviewable, and imposing filing windows and limits on parties that have instituted district court challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For second-window PGRs, proposals included presumptions of validity and filing time limits (e.g., within 12 months of receiving notice of infringement). Manager's amendments also limited who may file and allowed settlement; exact standards evolved during markup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue limitations for patent litigation (Specter amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Specter amendment limited venue in patent infringement and declaratory judgment actions to specified districts: (1) defendant's principal place of business or incorporation (or primary U.S. subsidiary for foreign defendants), (2) district where defendant committed substantial acts of infringement and has a regular and established physical facility comprising substantial operations, or (3) primary plaintiff residence if plaintiff is a qualifying micro-entity or university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also prohibits manufacturing venue by assignment/incorporation, provides for transfer in limited situations, and restricts venue choices against foreign defendants.
